verdict: Strategy lost $12.5B in a single quarter — almost all of it a $14.5B paper writedown of its Bitcoin stash as the price fell — while the actual software business grew 12% to $124M and lost only about $15M before the Bitcoin line.

kpis.label: Bitcoin loss
kpis.note: paper writedown — no Bitcoin sold for this loss, no cash out

segments.name: Software revenue
segments.note: The original business: analytics software — subscriptions ($58.9M), product support ($44.2M), licenses ($5.5M) and other services ($15.7M). Up 12% YoY as subscriptions keep replacing licenses.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — for Strategy this also covers the machinery of its Bitcoin treasury strategy.

opex.name: Unrealized Bitcoin loss
opex.note: Strategy holds Bitcoin and marks it to market price every quarter (accounting rule ASU 2023-08). Bitcoin's price fell in Q1, so the stash was written down by $14.5B. This is a paper loss — it reverses if the price recovers — and the filing puts it inside operating expenses.

follow100Note: Shrunk to $100 of software revenue, the Bitcoin writedown is about $11,630 — it dwarfs the software business, which is the story of this company.

takeaways.title: A paper loss, not a cash loss
takeaways.text: Bitcoin fell during the quarter, so accounting rules wrote the stash down by $14.5B. Strategy actually bought 89,599 more Bitcoin in Q1 for $7.3B and ended March holding 762,099.

takeaways.title: The software business is steady
takeaways.text: Software revenue grew 12% to $124M with a 67% gross margin — subscriptions ($59M) are now the biggest piece as licenses shrink. Before the Bitcoin line, the software business lost about $15M.

takeaways.title: Common holders bear it all
takeaways.text: After $230M of dividends on Strategy's preferred stock, the loss attributable to common stockholders was $12.77B, or $38.25 per share. A $1.9B tax benefit softened the headline loss.

oneTimers: The $14.5B Bitcoin loss is not a sale — it is a mark-to-market revaluation under accounting rule ASU 2023-08 (in force since January 1, 2025), which runs Bitcoin's price changes through earnings every quarter. It will be back next quarter, as a gain or a loss.
The writedown generated a $1.9B income-tax benefit — mostly deferred taxes, which reverse if Bitcoin's price recovers.
Between net loss and what common shareholders 'got': $229.5M of dividends on Strategy's preferred stock — leaving −$12,772.2M attributable to common stockholders.
otherDetail: Interest income exceeded interest expense by $1.8M, plus $3.1M of other income — net +$4.9M.
footerNote: Formerly MicroStrategy. The Bitcoin writedown sits in operating expenses, as filed.
